precepts.text: Casting all your care upon him, for he careth for you. Go before the Lord and spread the problem out as Hezekiah did.
precepts.point: Rabshakeh had cried in the Jews' language: let not Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord; make an agreement with me by a present and I will carry you to a land like your own; which of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of my hand? The people held their peace at the king's commandment.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Assyria had already taken the northern kingdom around 722 BC, and around 701 they came for Judah. Their ambassador was talking big: we are going to wipe the floor with you, destroy you and bring you into slavery. Then came a letter of threats. And look at what Hezekiah did with it: he “went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.” He took the letter, spread it out before him, and began to pray: “thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth”.

That is what Peter teaches: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” Sometimes we get in situations and fear comes upon us. Go before the Lord. Whatever the problem is, the Lord knows; go before him and spread it out before him, the way Hezekiah did.

And the Lord answered. Isaiah was not in the room when Hezekiah prayed, but the Lord told him to go to the king and say, “That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.” That is how you know Isaiah was a prophet. Hezekiah cast his care upon the Lord, and that same night one angel smote 185,000 Assyrians.

precepts.text: Hast not thou made an hedge about him? Put forth thine hand and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face. All that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. Satan can take your possessions and manipulate your environment, but not your actions. Job 2:7-9: he smote Job with boils and then his wife said, curse God, and die. Satan did not control her; he put the thought in the weaker vessel, since women give in to their emotions more than men, and she chose to act on it.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

precepts.text: The devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot to betray him. He put the thought in Judas's heart and Judas acted on it.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

precepts.text: Peter rebuked him, be it far from thee, Lord, and Christ said, get thee behind me, Satan, thou savourest not the things that be of God. Peter had good intentions, but even when good is present evil is there, and Christ spotted Satan from a distance without Peter knowing. Measure your intentions and words through the word of God, because Satan can whisper through your thoughts if your mind is not in tune with the scriptures.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

precepts.text: She goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, and meeteth them in every thought. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought: what is the outcome of this thought? In an argument with your husband, the thought says say this word and you can trigger him; filter it for godly intentions. 2 Corinthians 13:10: the power the Lord gave is to edification, and not to destruction. Someone's positive word may land negative because Satan knows what you are going through and uses their vessel; you choose to respond for edification or to bring contention, or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

precepts.text: If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. Doing well is a covenant with God's commandments: I will not watch, eat, touch, or taste that. Doing not well is a covenant with death, Satan's commandments; every disagreement with God's commandment is an agreement with Satan's. Agree to go past the alcohol limit and you let a spirit take your body; agree with the thought that you do not like that sister and you spread gossip through the body; agree with the hunger pains and the smell and a gluttony spirit is on you. A contract with the thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

precepts.text: Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind. Nobody is paid for this. If Christ is the brain of this operation, trust the men he set up who see from a level you cannot. Brothers and sisters get horny and antsy, ignore the counsel, and then ask the same leadership to counsel them after the fact, which is backwards, and nobody does that but us.
precepts.point: The vision is yet for an appointed time; at the end it shall speak, and not lie; though it tarry, wait for it, because it will surely come. Habakkuk, Ezra, the disciples, everyone asked when; do not worry, it is coming, so be ready. Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him, Esau; but the just shall live by his faith, by the words of the book of our fathers.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
Habakkuk said, “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. The watchman on the tower sees what the people below cannot. Peter gives the elders that charge: “Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof”.

Listen to the wording: taking the oversight. The leaders stand at a vantage point the flock cannot see. From the experience and the level they have reached over their years in the truth, they see what younger men and younger women do not, and God gave them revelation through the scriptures to see how to guide you. If we believe there is a God, and that Christ is the brain of this whole operation, then we are supposed to trust the men he set up.

But a lot of brothers and sisters in the congregation get horny and antsy and will not follow the counsel. Then they end up asking the same leadership whose oversight they did not trust to counsel them on the matter after the fact. That is completely backwards, and nobody does that but us. That is the negro mind.

“Not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind”. That is for the leadership: they feed the flock willingly and take the oversight because they love their people. Nobody is getting paid to do this. They do it of a ready mind, watching from the tower until the vision the Lord appointed comes.

precepts.text: All things are double, one against another, and he hath made nothing imperfect. Satan was created to do exactly what he does, and one thing establisheth the good of another. When Satan attacks and we are not devoured, we become better.
precepts.point: Even the worst things, like Job losing his kids, are to make us perfect. It is a hard saying, but without Satan our adversary we cannot become perfect.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another”. God created good, and he created evil also. He “hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, walking about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

“One thing establisheth the good or another”. What establishes the good of us and makes us perfect? When we go through temptation, when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Satan does devour some; some brothers and sisters get devoured. But those that are not devoured become better and become perfect. That is why Peter says “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect”. It is a hard saying, but without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job and his children's job to try us, and as they try us they make us better. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

So learn how to fight him and how to see him when he is attacking. See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say, get out of my mind, Satan. Don't wait until he puts the thought there and you act on it, and afterward you are like Judas, what did I do? That is why the scripture says be vigilant: vigilant means you are watching.

And “who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord's glory.

precepts.text: Gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. The same fire that destroys some men purifies the acceptable ones. When the ADL and government organizations attack, some will leave and some will come out pure gold.
precepts.point: Even the worst things, like Job losing his kids, are to make us perfect. It is a hard saying, but without Satan our adversary we cannot become perfect.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children. So the furnace of adversity in Sirach is the work of the adversary the devil in Peter.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through that fire, it doesn't destroy him. It makes him better; it purifies him. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it will destroy, and some men it will make perfect in the sight of God. When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some of you sisters will be up out of here: I ain't messing with them, the government say they a hate group. Some of you brothers will be gone too. But some of you will be purified and become that pure gold.

You have to go through adversity. Your enemy has to attack you; that is how you become better and how you become a better fighter. Then Peter's words come to pass: “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” Nobody wants to suffer, but the Lord says if you want the kingdom you have to suffer, and if you are acceptable, after you suffer you will get the kingdom. Suffering makes you perfect, establishes you, strengthens you until you are battle hardened like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years, and settles you within your spirit: it is what it is.

precepts.text: Be sober, be vigilant, because your adversary the devil walketh about seeking whom he may devour. The enemy looks for open doors and distracted people; the moment someone leaves the camp the Christian apologists show up to take them back into the world.
precepts.point: Now it is high time to awake out of sleep, for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Prepare for war mentally; with all this going on in the earth, staying spiritually asleep is madness.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
Waking out of sleep means staying awake: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

You have to stay sober and vigilant, because the enemy looks for open doors and distracted people. As soon as one of y’all gets distracted from the mission, they are coming. That is why every time somebody leaves, we see who shows up: the damn Christian apologists.

They take you all the way back into the world and have you speaking all manner of evil, but they are not telling you to prepare yourself mentally for what is to come. They are just trying to destroy what we are doing. They are not trying to save your soul. They say they are already saved; they are not saved from the nuclear missiles that are about to drop.

So the one who is asleep is the one the roaring lion devours. It is high time to wake up, stay sober, stay vigilant and stay on the mission, because the adversary is walking about looking for whoever drifts.

precepts.text: Your adversary the devil walketh about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
precepts.point: Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth therein, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed. Christ's grace is the platform to build on, so there is no going backwards.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.text: Ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder.
precepts.point: Come out from among them and be ye separate, and I will receive you and be a father unto you. The congregation becomes father and mother to those who come in with no parents to teach them.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. When the brothers teach on the street, that is what they tell our brothers and sisters: come out of the sinful lives you are living in, out of Babylon the great, out of these wicked holidays like Christmas. But if we tell them to come out of something, they have to come into something. They have to have something to say yes to, like righteously enjoying the commandments of the Lord through the high holy days. An organized nation thinks on all of these points and deals with the nation holistically.

They lose their wicked parents and wicked friends when they come in, so the Lord says “I will receive you”, and “will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters”. Your fathers out there did not teach you anything. Your mothers did not teach you anything. So the Lord gives you fathers and mothers in this truth.

That is why Peter says “Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder.” When our brothers and sisters come in, they are going to have to submit to the leadership, to the elders who now stand as their fathers and mothers.

When you are received, you are not abandoned or left out in the cold. You were lost, but now you are found: welcome home. Now we have belonging, now we are loved, wrapped in the Most High's care, and that makes you stand up with esteem and refuse to let mediocrity deter you from the righteous path.
